sections.h2: What should a McLeod County, MN owner know about property tax before selling?
sections.html:
Two offices decide what a parcel owes. The assessor picks the value and the class, and the Auditor-Treasurer in Glencoe converts those into a bill and collects it.

Before listing, confirm three items: the current half is paid, no special assessment is attached, and you know what happens to the homestead class at closing. Each can shift what a seller nets, and a phone call settles each one.

  • Auditor-Treasurer, 520 Chandler Avenue North, Glencoe: 320-864-1203 for payments and 320-864-1271 for tax balance questions.
  • County Assessor: 320-864-1254 for valuation, class and homestead forms.

sections.h2: Where is McLeod County and who lives in its homes?
sections.html:
McLeod County sits west of the Twin Cities in south central Minnesota. It covers 506 square miles, about 491 of them land, and it was created by the territorial legislature on March 1, 1856. Glencoe holds the courthouse, while Hutchinson has the most people. Biscay, Brownton, Lester Prairie, Plato, Silver Lake, Stewart and Winsted round out the list of cities. The South Fork of the Crow River crosses the upper middle of the county, and low rolling hills and small lakes mark the rest of the farmland.

The 2020 count was 36,771 people, and the July 2025 estimate is 36,631. Of the 16,162 housing units QuickFacts lists, 77.4% of occupied ones are owned. A typical owned home was worth $246,100 across 2020 to 2024, and a typical household brought in $80,084. Builders took out 206 permits in 2025. Census data for 2020 put 55.5% of residents in urban areas and 44.5% in rural areas, so a seller might hold a Hutchinson lot, a farmstead near Brownton or a lake cabin, and each is taxed in its own class.

sections.h2: When is McLeod County property tax due?
sections.html:
Regular real estate and personal property tax is due May 15 and October 15. Farmland follows a later calendar, and manufactured homes use their own dates. McLeod County lists the schedule this way:

McLeod County annual property tax due dates (McLeod County Auditor-Treasurer, Due Dates page)
Property typeFirst halfSecond half
Real estate and personal propertyMay 15October 15
Agricultural propertyMay 15November 15
Manufactured homesAugust 31November 15

Statements go out in March, with a statutory mailing deadline of March 31. Manufactured home statements are scheduled for June, with a July 15 deadline. An owner who has not received a statement still has to pay, so call the Auditor-Treasurer for a duplicate. A seller who is mid-transaction should ask for a copy early, because the buyer's lender and the title company will want to see the parcel number and the amount.

sections.h2: How can I pay McLeod County property tax?
sections.html:
The county offers six payment methods. Pick with the closing calendar in mind.

  • In person by check or cash at the Government Center in Glencoe.
  • By mail, made out to McLeod County Auditor-Treasurer. Mail needs a postmark by the due date, and the county cautions that servicing centers can stamp it two or three days after you drop it off.
  • Online or by phone with a credit card or eCheck. The card fee is 2.5% of the transaction. eChecks cost $1.50 under $10,000 and $10.00 above that.
  • The secure drop box in front of the Government Center. Anything inside at 8:00 a.m. counts as the previous day's business.
  • Direct debit from a bank account, which must be set up at least one month before the due date.
  • Mortgage escrow, where the lender pays from the account it holds.

In the online search, type just the numeric part of the parcel ID and pick the roll type from the drop-down.

sections.h2: What happens if a McLeod County tax payment is late?
sections.html:
Minnesota Statutes 279.01 sets the schedule. A half that is still open after its date picks up 2% on a homestead or 4% on other property, then the same again at the start of the next month, then 1% monthly through December. Ceilings are 8% for homestead and 12% for nonhomestead. McLeod County sends owners to the state sample tax statement for the current table.

A year becomes delinquent in the following calendar year, and interest and penalty then keep building each month while the parcel heads toward judgment and forfeiture. The office takes payments above or below the exact installment, and a short payment covers that year's penalty first. A one-time abatement is available when a mailed payment carries a postmark within one business day of the due date and the owner has not used that relief before.

sections.h2: Who sets my value in McLeod County, and how do I appeal it?
sections.html:
Sue Schulz is the McLeod County Assessor. Her office sets market value and class, and the Auditor-Treasurer applies the local rate to it. A deputy assessor and four appraisers divide the county by area. The deputy assessor handles Hutchinson plus every apartment and commercial parcel, an appraiser covers Glencoe, Lester Prairie and Winsted, and the staff page lists who covers each township and smaller city. The Department of Revenue requires every property to be viewed, and the county says a visit takes about 15 minutes or less. An owner can decline the inspection and the appraiser then judges value from outside.

Challenges move up three steps under Minnesota Statutes chapters 274 and 278:

  • Local board of appeal and equalization: your town board or city council sits sometime from April 1 to May 31 and wraps up within 20 days. Its combined reductions cannot cut the assessor's total by more than one percent.
  • County board: the commissioners and the auditor take what the local board left open. Owners who ignored a notice at the local level may be barred from this stage.
  • Tax Court or district court: file the petition and proof of service before the end of April in the year the bill is payable.

A call to the assessor with a few comparable sales is the cheapest first move.

sections.h2: Which relief programs can lower a McLeod County tax bill?
sections.html:
For most owners the homestead class is the biggest saving. McLeod County says occupying the property by December 1 lets an owner apply for the following year. A closing resets it: under 272.115 the assessor drops the homestead class after a transfer unless the buyer applies and qualifies. A buyer who forgets will see a bigger bill the next year, so raise it during negotiation.

The county's FAQ also covers state refunds. Someone who lived in the property as a homestead on January 2 may get a refund scaled to household income and tax paid, and a second, special refund exists where the bill jumped by more than 12 percent in a year. Form M-1PR claims both, and the Department of Revenue answers form questions at 651-296-4444.

sections.h2: How do taxes work when a McLeod County house sells?
sections.html:
Recording a deed in Minnesota depends on the tax record. Section 272.12 has the auditor look for delinquent taxes before moving the land on the books, and a recorder who skips that step commits a gross misdemeanor. A deed that conveys only part of a parcel needs the treasurer's word that this year's tax on the whole parcel is paid (272.121). Sales above $3,000 also need a certificate of value (272.115).

Find out from the closing agent how this year's tax will be split, and from your lender what becomes of any escrow balance. Special assessments for streets and similar improvements appear as a separate line on the statement and follow the benefit to the parcel, so ask the Auditor-Treasurer what remains unpaid on a parcel before you settle on a price.

The November Truth in Taxation notice previews next year's tax. It omits special assessments, and a passed referendum can raise the final number.

faqs.q: Which McLeod County office answers tax questions?
faqs.a: The Auditor-Treasurer handles bills and payments at 320-864-1203 or 320-864-1271, and the Assessor handles value, class and homestead at 320-864-1254. Both sit in the Government Center at 520 Chandler Avenue North in Glencoe.

faqs.q: What are the McLeod County property tax due dates?
faqs.a: Regular real estate is due May 15 and October 15. Agricultural property is due May 15 and November 15, and manufactured homes are due August 31 and November 15. Statements are mailed in March.

faqs.q: Can I pay McLeod County taxes by credit card?
faqs.a: Yes, online or by phone. The vendor adds 2.5% of the total for cards, and eChecks run $1.50 below $10,000 or $10.00 above. Cash, check, the drop box, direct debit and escrow are also accepted.

faqs.q: Does a McLeod County sale cancel the homestead classification?
faqs.a: It does for the next assessment year unless the buyer files a homestead application and qualifies. State law has the assessor strip the class after a transfer, and the owner is expected to report the sale within 30 days.

faqs.q: When must a McLeod County value dispute reach court?
faqs.a: The petition is due by April 30 of the payable year. Work through the local board in April or May and then the county board first, because skipping those steps after notice can cost you the right to appear.
